new.story: A 1995 Mexican 10 centavos from the nuevo peso reform series struck 1992-2009. The reverse shows a large 10¢ with the date above and the Mexico City mint mark below, framed by a border of points and beads taken from the Aztec Calendar Stone's Ring of Sacrifice. These stainless steel centavos were struck for everyday small change in the years after Mexico revalued the peso.

new.story: A British five pence dated 1992, struck in cupronickel for everyday circulation. The obverse shows Raphael Maklouf's crowned portrait of Elizabeth II with the date in the legend. The reverse carries the crowned thistle design marked FIVE PENCE. The Royal Mint at Llantrisant struck about 453 million five pence coins in 1992.

new: A 1973 10 cents from Singapore. Value side two stalks of rice, large 10, CENTS, 1973, SINGAPORE; the other side shows a crowned seahorse. Struck in cupronickel.
old: A 1973 10 cents from Singapore. Value side rice stalk left, large 10, CENTS, 1973, SINGAPORE, national arms and lion-fish on the obverse. Struck in cupronickel.
source: Numista N#1671 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces1671.html): Singapore 10 cents 1967-1985 (KM# 3, Schön# 3): obverse 'Denomination flanked by two stalks of paddy' (lettering 1974 SINGAPORE 10 CENTS); reverse 'Crowned Seahorse (Binomial Name: Hippocampus coronatus)'; engraver Stuart Devlin; copper-nickel 75/25; 1973 row 14 290 000 (matches the record). The story said 'national arms and lion-fish on the obverse'; this coin has no arms and the lionfish is the 50-cent design, so only that sentence is changed (same error as C250, fixed in changes_grok-bot_20261008-1103.jsonl). 'rice stalk left' rewritten as the entry's two stalks. [phase 2; confidence high]

new: A 1987 500 lire from Italy. The obverse shows female head of Italia; the reverse shows Quirinale Palazzo; Dioscuri, L. 500, Braille 500 on ring, wheat, date, R. Struck in bimetallic (bronzital center with an acmonital ring).
old: A 1987 500 lire from Italy. The obverse shows female head of Italia; the reverse shows Quirinale Palazzo; Dioscuri, L. 500, Braille 500 on ring, wheat, date, R. Struck in bimetallic (bronzesital center with an acmonital ring).
source: Numista N#302 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces302.html): Italy 500 lire 1982-2001 (KM# 111, Schön# 110): composition 'Bimetallic: bronzital centre in acmonital ring'; reverse 'a view of the Piazza del Quirinale, Rome, with small date in lower position. Value ("L.500") in Braille at top of the outer ring, as text at the bottom; plants on either sides' (lettering R 1987 L.500); obverse female head (Laura Cretara). The story misspelled the centre alloy as 'bronzesital'; the alloy is bronzital. Only that word was changed; the rest of the story matches the entry. [phase 2; confidence high]
